# H1_2: Abnormal Motion or Training Instability After Migration to Isaac Lab, What Did Practitioners Adjust?

> **Current answer:** The practitioner first converted the H1_2 URDF to USD and replaced the H1 environment model. The three handling steps reported were: increased number of joints, larger model, and increasing the number of iterative-solution from 4 to 400 to avoid abnormal motion; adding all upper-body joints to ground collision detection; and identifying that the acceleration reward proportion was too high, and suggesting to observe the reward on TensorBoard step by step. The user claims basic walking is implemented, but no field names, configuration, version, or curve are provided, so these can only be used as migration checklists and cannot be copied verbatim, such as the 400 or reward proportion.

## Possible causes

- The practitioner linked the abnormal motion to insufficient iteration counts after increasing the model size.
- The collision detection set does not cover all upper body joints; the acceleration reward weight is too large.

## Attempts

- Convert H1_2 URDF to USD and replace the H1 environment model; increase the number of iterative-solution from 4 to 400; add all upper-body joints to ground collision detection; observe the reward on TensorBoard.
